archiveTake: One of the easiest shows to recommend to someone getting into audio dramas: approachable, mysterious, and increasingly intense.
spoilerFreeReview: Tower 4 was the first audio drama that really pulled me into the medium. It will always have a special place in my heart for that reason. But beyond that, the show is just great. I really liked the characters, and the show does a good job of making you care about them. It starts out somewhat slow, but in later seasons the scope grows a lot and things start getting intense.

The show is great in that it doesn't always just tell you the truth. You have to figure things out alongside the characters. It's the good kind of mystery where you don't feel lost, but always feel like the answer is just around the corner.

My only real complaint is that it makes use of a lot of inner monologue, which I'm not a huge fan of. However, I think that also makes it great for beginner listeners who haven't gotten used to the medium yet. Tower 4 pulls it off really well, and since large parts of the show are spent with characters in isolation, it feels like a necessary evil.

I would strongly recommend this to new and old audio drama listeners alike. If you're looking for a mystery or just characters to fall in love with, this is a great show for you. It's one of my cleanest recommendations for anyone who's new to audio dramas and looking to get into the medium.
thoughts: Tower 4 will always mean a little more to me than most shows because it was the one that really pulled me into audio drama in the first place. Without it, I probably wouldn’t have gone looking for half the shows I ended up loving later.

I also think it’s unusually good as a first audio drama. The inner monologue can be a bit much for me personally, but it makes the story incredibly easy to follow while you’re still getting used to a format where you can’t rely on visuals. Once the mystery starts opening up, it gets much harder to put down.
